record.question: What material is commonly used for the X-ray tube anode in mammography?
record.explanation: Answer B: Molybdenum. Molybdenum is a common mammography anode target (with rhodium/tungsten also used depending on system and breast thickness). Source/context note: Target material is system-dependent; molybdenum is common but rhodium/tungsten may also be used. Reference: https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/bodyct; https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Contrast-Manual. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
